les: Elke klank begin by iets wat vibreer
kaps_punt: Vibrasies en klank. Musiekinstrumente maak geluide deur vibrasies; die klank beweeg altyd uitwaarts vanaf die deel wat vibreer; ons kan vibrasies voel of hoor; die vibrasies beweeg deur materiale soos lug, water, plastiek, metaal en hout.

items.bewering: Sit jou hand plat teen jou keel en neurie 'n bekende wysie. Onder jou vingers voel jy hoe iets in jou keel vinnig bewe.
items.blok: Voel dit self teen jou keel
items.bron: NHS Fife Speech and Language Therapy, 'Tuning in to your resonance' (nhsfife.org): a hand placed gently on the throat while humming feels noticeable vibration. NIDCD, 'How does the human body produce voice and speech' (nidcd.nih.gov): voice is produced when air from the lungs sets the vocal folds vibrating; Weill Cornell voice pages: more than 100 cycles a second, so 'vinnig' holds.

items.bewering: Hou nou op met neurie en laat jou hand op dieselfde plek bly. Die bewing hou saam met die klank op, en jou hand voel niks meer nie. Begin weer neurie en die bewing kom dadelik terug.
items.blok: Voel dit self teen jou keel
items.bron: NIDCD voice-production explainer (nidcd.nih.gov) and Voice Foundation, 'Understanding voice production' (voicefoundation.org): the hummed sound IS the vocal-fold vibration driven by airflow, so the vibration starts and stops with the sound. No source tests the stop-start sequence as an observation, but it follows directly from the documented mechanism and makes no further claim.

items.bewering: Om te vibreer beteken om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg. Die beweging gaan net oor 'n baie klein entjie.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'vibrate': to move from side to side very quickly and with small movements. Dictionary.com: to move to and fro or up and down quickly and repeatedly. Dutch cognate 'vibreren/trillen' (Wiktionary, Vocabulary.com): to move back and forth rapidly.

items.bewering: Jy kan die vibrasie in jou keel en dié van 'n trom se vel voel.
items.bron: NHS Fife (throat, as above). Penn State News, 'Probing question: why are some deaf people able to play instruments?' (psu.edu): Evelyn Glennie learned to feel her drums through her body; deaf dancers feel vibration through the floor.

items.bewering: Mense wat nie kan hoor nie, kan vibrasies voel, en party van hulle beleef musiek so.
items.bron: Penn State News (psu.edu), as above: feeling the vibrations of sound is one way many deaf people, including those deaf from birth, experience music; Glennie quoted feeling low sounds in her legs and feet. Seattle Times archive, 'Percussionist Glennie hears with her body'. 'Party van hulle' is appropriately narrow.

items.bewering: Ander vibrasies is te klein om te voel, en dan hoor jy hulle net.
items.bron: arXiv 2004.13462, 'When Hearing Defers to Touch': at about 300 Hz the hand's touch threshold is about 0.1 micrometre of displacement, while hearing detects displacements as small as 0.1 nanometre, about a thousand times smaller. SFU Handbook for Acoustic Ecology, 'Threshold of hearing', agrees on the ear's extreme sensitivity.

items.bewering: Musiekinstrumente maak hulle klank deur vibrasies: iets in of op die instrument vibreer.
items.bron: DOSITS (University of Rhode Island), 'How are sounds made?' (dosits.org): sound is made by vibration, for example a drum's flexible skin. 'In of op' correctly covers wind instruments, where the vibrating part is the air column inside.

items.bewering: Slaan 'n trom en die vel bo-op begin vinnig op en af vibreer.
items.bron: DOSITS, 'How are sounds made?' (dosits.org): striking a drum sets its membrane vibrating, compressing and expanding the air next to it. 'Op en af' fits a drum played with its skin on top, which is what the sentence says.

items.bewering: Pluk 'n kitaar se snaar en jy sien die snaar self vibreer.
items.bron: Les Paul Foundation, 'Subject Based Activities' (les-paul.com): pluck a string and look at it move; lower and higher strings move differently. Physics Forums and UMD lecture-demonstration pages describe the visible blur of a plucked string. Sources are modest, but the claim is only that the motion is visible, not that its shape is.

items.bewering: In albei gevalle vibreer die deel eerste, en die klank kom daarvan af.
items.bron: 'Eerste' here gives an order of events (vibration first, sound from it), not a historical first. DOSITS (dosits.org): the vibrating skin produces the pressure wave. Logged as superlatief because the word appears; no softening needed.

items.bewering: 'n Ding vibreer nie sommer vanself nie: iemand of iets moet dit aan die beweeg kry.
items.bron: DOSITS (dosits.org): the vibration comes from striking, plucking or blowing. NIDCD: the vocal folds vibrate because air from the lungs drives them. 'Iemand of iets' is wide enough for wind, a machine or flowing air.

items.bewering: Waar jy ook al rondom 'n trom staan, hoor jy hom wanneer iemand daarop slaan. Jy hoor hom voor en agter die trom en aan albei kante. Die klank kies nie een rigting nie, en dit gaan na alle kante toe.
items.blok: Die klank gaan na alle kante toe
items.bron: Britannica video 'Propagation of sound waves' (britannica.com): sound travels in all directions from a source. Science Learning Hub (sciencelearn.org.nz), 'Animated ripple pattern': sound radiates out in all directions from a vibrating source. A drum is not perfectly even in every direction, but the lesson only claims you hear it all round, which is true.

items.bewering: Dit beweeg altyd van die vibrerende vel af na buite toe.
items.blok: Die klank gaan na alle kante toe
items.bron: DOSITS (dosits.org): the wave moves outward from the drum surface. Britannica (as above).

items.bewering: Dit voel asof 'n dingetjie van die trom af na jou toe vlieg. Dit is nie wat gebeur nie, en niks vlieg van die trom af weg nie.
items.blok: Niks vlieg van die trom af na jou toe nie
items.bron: The Physics Classroom, 'Sound: Nature of a sound wave' (physicsclassroom.com): waves transport energy, not matter. Penn State Acoustics and Vibration Animations (acs.psu.edu/drussell): the disturbance travels, not the particles.

items.bewering: Die vel stoot die lug wat teen hom staan, 'n klein entjie weg. Daardie lug stoot die lug langsaan en gaan dan terug na sy plek. So loop die stoot van lug tot lug tot by jou oor. Die lug self bly waar dit is en waai nie na jou toe nie.
items.blok: Niks vlieg van die trom af na jou toe nie
items.bron: The Physics Classroom (physicsclassroom.com): air particles vibrate about a fixed position and pass the disturbance on by particle-to-particle interaction. Penn State acoustics animations (acs.psu.edu/drussell). Checking the mapping: each bit of air is pushed, pushes the next and goes back, so the push travels and the air does not. A learner reasoning further reaches 'the push travels, the air does not', which is correct. The simplification (one push, where the real motion is a repeated back-and-forth) does not lead anywhere false at this level.

items.bewering: Lug is die gewone pad, en die trom se klank kom so by jou uit.
items.bron: DOSITS (dosits.org): the drum skin compresses and expands the surrounding air, producing the wave that reaches the listener.

items.bewering: Vibrasies loop ook deur materiale soos hout, metaal, plastiek en water.
items.bron: cyberphysics.co.uk, 'Bell jar': sound needs a material medium, whether solid, liquid or gas. Questacon (questacon.edu.au), 'Sound under water': sound travels through water. Phys-L archive, Feb 2005, msg00427 (phys-l.org): sound travels through a wooden table.

items.bewering: Lê jou oor plat op 'n houttafel en tik lig met een vinger so ver as wat jou arm kan reik. Dieselfde ligte tik klink harder deur die hout as wanneer jou kop regop is.
items.bron: Phys-L physics-teachers' list archive, Feb 2005, msg00427 (phys-l.org): the listener 'will barely be able to hear the sound when sitting upright', and with an ear to the table 'the sound IS louder than the sound observed while listening in the air'. The same post warns that the sound does not grow louder as it travels; the gain comes from more energy reaching the ear through contact. The lesson claims only the observed comparison, which is exactly what the source supports. It does not claim the wood amplifies, and should not be revised to.

items.bewering: Dieselfde gebeur wanneer iemand aan 'n metaalhek of 'n plastiekpyp tik.
items.bron: Phys-L msg00427 (as above): the effect comes from energy entering the solid and reaching the ear through direct contact, so it applies to any solid you put your ear against, metal and plastic included. Note for the writer, not a fault: the sentence relies on 'Dieselfde' to carry the condition that your ear is against the gate or pipe. Read on its own, it does not say so.

items.bewering: Klank loop ook deur water, soos wanneer jy met jou kop onder die water luister terwyl iemand teen die bad tik.
items.bron: Questacon, the Australian national science centre, 'Sound under water' (questacon.edu.au): with your head under the bath water, tapping on the tub is heard, and louder. Exploratorium (annex.exploratorium.edu, sonar 'Try this') explains the extra loudness through the skull, but agrees the sound reaches you through the water.

items.bewering: Klank het altyd iets nodig om deur te beweeg. Daar moet 'n materiaal soos lug, water, plastiek, metaal of hout in die pad wees. Sonder so 'n materiaal kan die klank nie by jou uitkom nie.
items.bron: cyberphysics.co.uk, 'Bell jar': as air is pumped out, the ringing fades while the clapper is still visibly moving, so sound cannot travel through a vacuum. 'Altyd' holds.

items.bewering: Jou buiteoor is die deel wat jy aan die kant van jou kop sien, saam met 'n klein gangetjie, die gehoorgang. Dit vang die klank en lei dit na binne.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital, 'Anatomy and physiology of the ear' (nationwidechildrens.org): the outer ear includes the pinna or auricle (the outside part of the ear) and the external auditory canal. Wikipedia, 'Outer ear': the auricle plus the ear canal, which gathers sound and focuses it on the eardrum. Some sources (BATOD) also count the eardrum as part of the outer ear; the lesson's two-part reading is the commoner one and is not wrong.

items.bewering: Aan die einde van die gehoorgang sit 'n dun velletjie wat styf gespan is. Ons noem dit die trommelvlies, en die klank laat daardie velletjie vibreer.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: StatPearls, 'Anatomy, head and neck, ear: tympanic membrane' (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK448117): the eardrum separates the ear canal from the middle ear, its larger part (the pars tensa) is taut, and it vibrates when sound reaches it. Nationwide Children's Hospital (as above).

items.bewering: By die trom kom die klank van die vibrasie af, en hier is dit andersom.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Checking the mapping: a drum skin vibrates and makes sound, and the eardrum is made to vibrate by sound. StatPearls (NBK448117) uses the same drum comparison for the tympanic membrane. Andersom (the order reversed) is exactly right, and the comparison does not suggest the eardrum makes sound. It holds.

items.bewering: Agter die velletjie gee die klein gehoorbeentjies die vibrasie aan tot by die binneoor.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital (nationwidechildrens.org): three small connected bones, the malleus, incus and stapes, send the sound waves to the inner ear. Vanderbilt Health Library, 'Anatomy and physiology of the ear', agrees.

items.bewering: Die binneoor stuur 'n boodskap na jou brein, en dan hoor jy die trom.
items.blok: Hoe die klank by jou oor inkom
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital (nationwidechildrens.org): the inner ear turns sound waves into electrical impulses, which the auditory nerve carries to the brain, where they are interpreted as sound.

items.bewering: vibreer: Om baie vinnig heen en weer te beweeg.
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries and Dictionary.com, 'vibrate' (as above). Read alone, it is accurate. It leaves out 'small movements', which the study block gives, but it is not false without it.

items.bewering: buiteoor: Die deel van jou oor wat jy aan die kant van jou kop sien, saam met die gehoorgang.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital; Wikipedia, 'Outer ear' (as above). True read alone, and it matches the study block.

items.bewering: gehoorgang: Die klein gangetjie in jou buiteoor wat na die trommelvlies loop.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Outer ear'; Radiopaedia, 'External ear': the canal runs from the auricle to the eardrum and is part of the outer ear. True read alone, and consistent with the buiteoor entry.

items.bewering: trommelvlies: 'n Dun velletjie in jou oor wat vibreer wanneer klank dit tref.
items.bron: StatPearls NBK448117 (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). True read alone.

items.bewering: gehoorbeentjies: Drie klein beentjies agter die trommelvlies wat die vibrasie verder aangee.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital (nationwidechildrens.org): three bones, the malleus, incus and stapes, in the middle ear behind the eardrum, which pass the vibration to the inner ear. 'Drie' is correct.

items.bewering: binneoor: Die deel diep in jou oor wat boodskappe na jou brein stuur.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital (nationwidechildrens.org): the inner ear sends impulses to the brain through the auditory nerve. It also sends balance signals, and the entry's wording covers both. True read alone.

opsomming: All 32 checkable claims hold against web sources, including the six glossary entries read on their own; the lesson has no historical superlative, and both comparisons (the push passed from air to air, and the ear as the drum in reverse) map correctly. One wording point, not a fault: 'Dieselfde gebeur' leaves the metal-gate and plastic-pipe sentence relying on the table sentence for the condition that your ear is against the material.
